eu_vat_rules.text: Standard rate must be at least 15% with no maximum (Art. 97 VAT Directive). Since the 2022 reform (Directive (EU) 2022/542) Member States may apply up to two reduced rates of at least 5% to the 24 categories of Annex III, one super-reduced rate below 5% and one zero rate to at most seven categories covering basic needs (e.g., foodstuffs, medicines, pharmaceutical products); some derogations allow parking rates of at least 12%.

reduced_rate_goods_general_note.text: Across Member States, reduced or super-reduced rates are most commonly applied to foodstuffs (often with a lower rate for basic staples), medicines and pharmaceutical products, books and newspapers, water supply, passenger transport, accommodation and, in several countries, restaurant food. Alcohol, sugary soft drinks and most other goods are taxed at the standard rate. Energy treatment varies by country and has changed often since 2022 (e.g., Spain's temporary 2026 cut; Portugal's 6% on electricity consumption within limits; Slovakia 19% on electricity; Italy 10% on domestic electricity and gas). See consumption[].reduced_rate_examples for verified country examples (DE, FR, ES, IT, PT, NL, AT, RO, SK, FI).

context.official_table_status: The DG TAXUD 'VAT rates applied in the Member States' PDF downloadable from the Commission is still the 2020 edition; the Commission now refers users to the Taxes in Europe Database (TEDB) and the Your Europe table, which is used here (last checked 2026-07-13).

scenario_guidance.status: methodology suggestion, not a sourced figure
scenario_guidance.text: VAT paid on a basket = sum(spend_i * r_i / (1 + r_i)) since EU shelf prices include VAT. Conservador: apply the lowest applicable reduced/super-reduced rate to food and essentials and the standard rate only to clearly standard-rated categories; Provável: map each spending category to its typical rate (examples per country); Elevado: standard rate to everything except categories verified as reduced. For labour taxes, the OECD 'income_tax_plus_employee_ssc_pct_gross_wage' at the average wage is a reasonable 'Provável' benchmark for a single average earner; the tax wedge (which adds employer SSC) is an upper-bound view of the total labour tax burden.
